VERDICT 2026-08-01 (AC3 + AC4, from Erik's pasted live output — 85 rows, year=2023, ran via SQL analytics endpoint / Option B T-SQL). RANKING-CHANGE VERDICT: YES. AC3 MET (>=5 materials: 85 rows at bottleneck stage). AC4: NOT a null result — weighting materially re-ranks. 68 of 85 materials changed rank (rank_delta != 0); 17 unchanged. Max |rank_delta| = 25 (Hafnium: plain 34 -> weighted 59, moved DOWN under weighting). Biggest DOWN movers (weighting makes them LESS relatively risky than plain concentration suggests): Hafnium -25 (34->59), Natural Cork -23 (46->69), Helium -20 (37->57), Beryllium -18 (28->46), Neon -11 (43->54), Rhenium -11 (52->63), Silica Sand -11 (67->78), Zirconium -9 (66->75) — consistent with supply from better-governed / lower-trade-friction regions (WGI*t < 1 compresses their HHI more than peers). Biggest UP movers (weighting makes them MORE relatively risky): Tin +16 (53->37), Natural Teak Wood +15 (40->25), Cobalt +12 (38->26), Tantalum +12 (65->53), Phosphate Rock +11 (60->49), Sapele Wood +11 (47->36), Tungsten +6 (23->17) — classic weak-governance / conflict-mineral / tropical-forestry supply chains (DRC cobalt/tin/tantalum), exactly the signal DEC-001 Option B was designed to surface. Top-10 heavy rare earths (Yttrium, Ytterbium, Dysprosium, Thulium, Holmium, Europium, Lutetium, Erbium, Terbium, Gadolinium) tie at rank 1/1 — single-source (plain HHI = 1.0, weighted 0.552 = WGI*t for that supplier), identical values across all 10, so no rank movement but largest absolute delta (-0.4479). hhi_value_delta: ALL 85 NEGATIVE (weighted < plain universally) — min -0.4479 (the 10 rare earths), max -0.0275 (Gold). CORRECTS the verdict template's 'expected: increases' prediction: that was a misreading of the weight ranges (WGI in [0,1] is a weight that COMPRESSES, not inflates; only export-restricted t>1 with high WGI could push weighted > plain, and no material's dominant supplier hits that). The universal decrease is the mathematically expected behavior, NOT a data anomaly. The weighting's value is in RE-RANKING by governance quality, not in inflating absolute risk magnitude — the report should frame it that way (governance+trade weighting reorders material risk while compressing absolute concentration). incomplete_wgi_coverage = TRUE for 12 materials (partial governance subset, HHI understated): Hydrogen, Gallium, Coking Coal, Natural Teak Wood, Tin, Iron Ore, Indium, Neon, Silica Sand, Talc, Selenium, Sulphur. CAVEAT for the report: two big UP-movers (Tin +16, Natural Teak Wood +15) are in this incomplete-coverage set, so their upward move may be UNDERSTATED (NULL-wgi/Taiwan suppliers dropped from both sides of the comparison; true full-supplier risk likely higher). Sensitivity query NOT run — primary shows clear movement, so the null-result robustness check is not needed. The verdict above is the AC3/AC4 record in task notes.
